content:
Russia has released American Stephen Hubbard, who had been detained in the country since 2022, President Donald Trump announced Wednesday, Oct. 21.

Hubbard, a retired teacher in his 70s, was living in Ukraine when Russia invaded in February 2022. He was captured and taken to Moscow, where he was convicted of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine and sentenced to nearly seven years. The U.S. State Department designated him as wrongfully detained in January 2025.

"Stephen is on his way back home and will soon be with his family," Trump said in a post on Truth Social. "Welcome home Stephen, it's great to have you back." Russian state media reported that President Vladimir Putin announced the release, with Hubbard at Pulkovo Airport in St. Petersburg. Trump said the United States did not make a prisoner "swap" to secure his freedom, and criticized the prior administration for failing to bring him home.

The release came as U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin in St. Petersburg on Wednesday, a day after Witkoff held a summit with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Norway. According to CNN, Witkoff described the Norway meeting as productive and pressed Putin to consider resuming trilateral Russia-U.S.-Ukraine talks. The agenda also included restoring U.S.-Russia economic cooperation, a possible meeting with China to discuss Ukraine, Russia's potential role in resolving the war in Iran, and possible Russian fertilizer exports to the United States. Jared Kushner, who has been involved in the negotiations, was expected to join remotely after coming down with the flu.

The diplomatic backdrop is contentious: in recent days Trump has eased sanctions on Moscow and said the United States would import Russian diesel to lower fuel prices — moves that have drawn bipartisan criticism as favoring Putin over Zelensky, according to USA Today.

What it means here: Webb County sends its sons and daughters into uniform at high rates, and families on this border know what it means to wait years for someone to come home. Whatever the politics of the negotiations, one American family gets its reunion.

Sources: CNN (Oct. 21, 2026); USA Today (Oct. 21, 2026); NPR (Oct. 21, 2026).

— Walter Webb & Willa Webb, News Anchors, Webb Watch 956

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: Russia freed American teacher Stephen Hubbard, detained since 2022, President Trump announced Oct. 21 — as U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg to press for an end to the war in Ukraine.
title: American teacher Stephen Hubbard freed from Russian detention as U.S. envoy meets Putin in St. Petersburg
